Commit e839e85cb3b825438e1ffdab316de6b8942cdc08 (HEAD of /home/user/taskdeck/target/work/core). Frozen copy: /home/user/taskdeck/target/work/check-security-c-ports. My probes are in crates/taskdeck-core/tests/sec_probe.rs, which is clock-free and fails as reported, and tests/sec_scratch.rs, which reads a clock and is only for timing. Neither should go into W as is.

What I covered:
- I read all of src/ics.rs and src/overlay.rs.
- I ran hand-made inputs with today's window (60 days back, 400 forward) and stayed under the 8 MiB fetch cap. The inputs covered:
  - RRULE parts: BYDAY, BYSETPOS, FREQ, COUNT, INTERVAL, and ancient DTSTART.
  - VTIMEZONE observance counts and resolve cost.
  - EXDATE/RDATE list lengths.
  - RECURRENCE-ID overrides with shared UIDs.
  - DURATION extremes, distinct undefined TZIDs, and sort ties.
  - OverlayEvent arithmetic on unsealed JSON.
- I checked by reading, with no fault found:
  - Unfolding and max_lines.
  - max_depth, using a Vec stack rather than recursion.
  - max_events.
  - Quoted-colon splitting.
  - Char-boundary slicing in read_utc_offset and BYDAY.
  - Every chrono date step in expand, days_in, week_start_of and nth_weekday.
  - apply_set_pos indexing.
  - read_duration_minutes' checked arithmetic.
  - span_minutes' range.
  - wall_time for UTC times before 1970 (Instant::MIN is 1970).
- I compared overlay ymd with chrono's %Y for years outside 0..9999 by hand and found them equal.

Not covered:
- weather.rs and compile::{trim, detab}.
- The FetchStatus.at RFC 3339 round trip for odd forms (leap second, lowercase 't', space separator). By reading, chrono's parser is the same for Local and FixedOffset.
- Peak memory of a VTIMEZONE at the max_lines limit (about 33,000 observances × 1000 points), which I estimate at about 1 GB but did not measure.
- Running the gate.

All the findings are inherited unchanged from today's src/ics.rs (lines 837, 1225, 1333, 1394, 744) and src/subscriptions.rs (line 238).
unreproduced: Peak memory from a VTIMEZONE at the max_lines limit (about 33,000 observances with DAILY rules, about 3.3e7 transition points) would be about 1 GB. I extrapolated this from 10^7 points at 10,000 observances and did not measure it.
EXDATE matching costs starts × exdates (ics.rs:1382). With 1000 starts and 500,000 EXDATEs that is about 5e8 comparisons. I did not time it on its own.

Problems::note with distinct TZIDs and a long common prefix (for example 10 KB) should get much worse than the 2.45 s I measured, because each string comparison is a long memcmp. I did not time it near the 8 MiB cap.

low.title: Zone resolution is a linear scan over an unbounded transition list: a 1.1 MB file takes 178 s, and an 8 MiB file would take hours
low.clause: brief c2 Tests 'in bounded time'; Limits doc (ics.rs:117-119)
low.repro:
Same file sec_probe.rs. Run: cargo test --locked -p taskdeck-core --release --test sec_probe b_zone  -> FAILED (proptest's 30 s timeout).

fn zone_scan() -> String { let mut s = String::from("BEGIN:VCALENDAR
BEGIN:VTIMEZONE
TZID:Z
"); for i in 0..10_000 { s.push_str(&format!("BEGIN:STANDARD
DTSTART:20250101T{:02}{:02}{:02}
TZOFFSETFROM:+0100
TZOFFSETTO:+0100
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY
END:STANDARD
", i / 3600, i / 60 % 60, i % 60)); } s.push_str("END:VTIMEZONE
BEGIN:VEVENT
DTSTART;TZID=Z:20261001T090000
EXDATE;TZID=Z:"); s.push_str(&vec!["20000101T090000"; 400_000].join(",")); s.push_str("
END:VEVENT
END:VCALENDAR
"); s }
(inside the proptest! block above) #[test] fn b_zone_transition_scan_returns_in_bounded_time(_x in Just(())) { let (from, until) = window(); let text = zone_scan(); prop_assert!(text.len() < 8 * 1024 * 1024); let _ = parse(&text, from, until, Limits::default(), &FixedZone(0)); }

Measured in release (scratch test with a clock), 10,000 observances: 0 EXDATEs 1.87 s; 1,000 EXDATEs (1.07 MB) 48.4 s; 4,000 EXDATEs (1.11 MB) 177.7 s. That is about 44 ms per zoned time, so the 400,000 EXDATEs above would take about 5 h. Cause: Zones::build (ics.rs:737-749) keeps up to max_occurrences_per_event (1000) transition points per observance, and nothing limits the number of observances (only max_lines does). Each resolve (ics.rs:768-775) then runs .rev().find over every point, which here is 10^7 points of about 32 bytes, roughly 320 MB held. The same scan runs for each DTSTART, DTEND, RDATE, EXDATE and RECURRENCE-ID value, and nothing limits how many of those a single line can list.

low.title: RECURRENCE-ID overrides bypass max_occurrences_per_event: a 1 MB file peaks at 1.16 GB of memory before parse cuts the result to 50,000
low.clause: Limits::max_occurrences_per_event ('Most occurrences one event may put in the window'); brief c2 'bounded'

Clock-free test (append to sec_probe.rs). Run: cargo test --locked -p taskdeck-core --release --test sec_probe g_overrides  -> FAILED, 50 > 35.

#[test] fn g_overrides_multiply_past_the_per_event_limit() { let (from, until) = window(); let limits = Limits { max_occurrences_per_event: 5, max_occurrences: 1_000_000, ..Limits::default() }; let mut text = String::from("BEGIN:VCALENDAR
"); for _ in 0..2 { text.push_str("BEGIN:VEVENT
UID:u
DTSTART:20261001T090000
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY
END:VEVENT
"); } for d in 1..=5 { text.push_str(&format!("BEGIN:VEVENT
UID:u
RECURRENCE-ID:2026100{d}T090000
DTSTART:20261001T100000
DURATION:PT1M
RRULE:FREQ=DAILY
END:VEVENT
")); } text.push_str("END:VCALENDAR
"); let parsed = parse(&text, from, until, limits, &FixedZone(0)).expect("a calendar"); assert!(parsed.occurrences.len() <= 7 * limits.max_occurrences_per_event, "{}", parsed.occurrences.len()); }

With default limits, measured as peak VmHWM of the scratch probe /home/user/taskdeck/target/work/check-security-c-ports/crates/taskdeck-core/tests/sec_scratch.rs fn c_overrides (run its release binary with OVN=461 and read /proc/<pid>/status VmHWM): the input is one DAILY series plus 461 overrides with UID u, each override with RRULE:FREQ=DAILY, DURATION:P400D and a 200-char SUMMARY plus 300-char DESCRIPTION of U+10348. It is 996,500 bytes and peaks at 1,161,756 KB, against 2,972 KB for OVN=1. Cause: ics.rs:1395-1396 extends `out` with each override's own expansion (up to cap+400) and then hits `continue`, which skips the per-event check at 1399. One series event therefore builds about 461×1200 Occurrences, each holding cloned strings, before parse's take(room) at ics.rs:226.

low.title: DURATION near i64::MAX overflows in spread: debug builds panic, release builds return an Occurrence with end < start
low.clause: Occurrence doc (ics.rs:55-57: 'end ... is never below start'); task: no panic, and both builds should read the same bytes the same way

Append to sec_probe.rs:
